open-question.question: What does the open-question tool's `remove` do when a block passed to it as an undermined dependent exists but carries no `<recommendation>` element?
open-question.recommendation: A named dependent is reconciled by the same per-block strip primitive as a tagged one, and that primitive already reports no change on a block carrying no recommendation half, so no new rule, output mode, or refusal is needed; nothing is lost, since a block with no pick has no pick to be stale and a tag naming a pick-less block is the state the tool tolerates everywhere else until that block is answered, while seeding a cascade from it would clear picks the runner never judged.
open-question.alternative: The call is accepted and makes its one write. The named block, holding no <recommendation>, goes through the same per-block primitive as every other dependent, which deletes whatever of the recommendation half it holds and reports no change when that is nothing (in a tool-written document a <depends-on> or <applied-principle> occurs only beside a <recommendation>, so such a block is left exactly as it stands, alternatives and all). Because nothing was deleted from it, it seeds no transitive strip: a block whose <depends-on> names it is left as it is. The removal of the answered block and the reconciliation of every other tagged or named dependent proceed in the same write, and the tool prints nothing, as a mutator does on success. This is the behaviour strip --recommendation already has on a bare or alternatives-only block. It needs no new rule: the named block takes the path every dependent already takes, whose primitive already reports no change on a block carrying no pick, so the tool's contract sentence and its output contract stay as they are and a runner that names a block whose pick was cleared earlier is never blocked. A name that matches no standing pick passes without a trace, since nothing in the commit diff shows it, so a runner that misread the standing picks, or that names from a view not showing which blocks carry one, gets no signal; and a pick that depends on the named block through a <depends-on> tag keeps standing until that block is answered, although the answer was judged to bear on the block it assumed.

The call is accepted and makes its one write. The named block itself is left as it stands (nothing of the recommendation half to delete), but it is treated as reconciled whether or not anything was deleted from it: every block whose <depends-on> names it is stripped as by strip --recommendation, keeping its alternatives, and that strip runs transitively exactly as it does from a block the call did strip. The tool prints nothing. The rule the tool states becomes that the strip runs over the dependents of every block removed, stripped, or named by the call. Strip on doubt reaches the whole chain in one write: a pick formed on an assumption about a block the answer was judged to undermine is cleared now rather than standing until that block is answered, so the answer sweep cannot record it in the meantime. It clears picks the runner never judged, one hop beyond its naming and from a block nothing was deleted from, widening the strip past the answer's judged bearing and costing each of those blocks a recommendation re-run; and a tag naming a pick-less block is a state the tool already tolerates everywhere else (walk ignores it, strip --recommendation leaves it, embed accepts a target without a pick), so this one call would reconcile what every other call leaves standing.

The call is accepted and makes its one write exactly as in Silent no-op: the named pick-less block is left as it stands, it seeds no transitive strip, and the removal and every other reconciliation proceed. In addition the tool prints one line on stderr naming the block and saying it carried no <recommendation>, and exits 0. The runner learns, at the one point no commit diff can show it, that its judgment named a block with no standing pick, without the write being blocked or the fold left stranded. It breaks the tool's output contract that a mutator prints nothing on success, which every runtime site restates in its one contract sentence, and hands the hand-answer skills a stderr line they must either relay or swallow, a choice that touches what the skill tells the user after it has cleared picks.

The call is accepted and makes its one write as in Silent cascade seed: the named pick-less block is left as it stands and its tagged dependents are stripped transitively as though it had been stripped. The tool also prints one line on stderr naming the block and saying it carried no <recommendation>, and exits 0. It pairs the widest strip on doubt with visibility of the runner's miss: nothing assuming the named block survives the write, and the runner still hears that the name itself matched no standing pick. It carries both costs at once: the output-contract break and the relay choice it forces on the skills, and a strip reaching blocks the runner never judged from a block nothing was deleted from, each of them costing a recommendation re-run.

The call fails with one Error: line on stderr naming the block and saying it carries no <recommendation>, exit status 1, and the document left byte-for-byte unchanged: the answered block is not removed and no tagged or named dependent is reconciled. The runner corrects the call by dropping that name and runs it again. This is the pattern check_recorded_option already applies to an --option naming none of the answered block's alternatives. A name that matches no standing pick is treated as a sign that the runner's view or judgment of the standing picks was off, and is caught loudly at the one point it can be caught, so the tool never silently absorbs an undermined-pick judgment formed against the wrong block. The refusal lands after the fold, so the decision is already recorded in requirements.md while the answered block still stands, and the whole write, the removal and every other dependent's reconciliation, waits on a corrected re-run; whether this is a rare misjudgment or a routine occurrence depends on the means by which the runner sees the standing picks, since a view that does not distinguish a picked block from a pick-less one makes every hand answer liable to the refusal.

open-question.question: After a hand answer has cleared the standing picks of other open questions, does the hand-answer skill tell the user which questions lost their pick, beside its one `Answer recorded.` status line?
open-question.recommendation: Every pick the write clears is recorded in the answer commit's diff and re-picked by the next recommendation pass through its own filter, and a wrong strip costs one re-pick whether or not it was announced, so a console line or body trailer would change no action while breaking the one-status-line rule or the lifted-line body contract; judgment-cleared picks are treated exactly as tag-cleared ones already are.
open-question.alternative: Both hand-answer skills keep their reporting step as it stands: the one fixed line `Answer recorded.` plus the existing advisory about new questions the answer may have raised, with nothing printed about any pick the write cleared, whether cleared by the runner's judgment, by a `<depends-on>` tag, or transitively. The answer commit's diff and the next run of the recommendation pass stay the only record, now and later; the tool's print contract and the CLAUDE.md invariant that stripped dependents get no console advisory are left untouched. Keeps the terse-reporting rule and the "stripped dependents get no console advisory" invariant whole, with no change to the tool's print contract, the skills' reporting steps, their tests, or CLAUDE.md; the judgment-cleared picks are treated exactly as tag-cleared ones already are. The judgment step is the one part of the cascade that reads the answer rather than a tag, and its result reaches the user only by opening the commit diff or when the next recommendation pass silently re-picks the stripped blocks, so a pick cleared on a misreading is caught late or never, and a user who disagrees with a strip has nothing at hand to disagree with.

Beside `Answer recorded.`, the skill prints a second fixed identifier-free line (such as `Standing picks cleared.`; a count is one variant within this option) only when the runner passed at least one undermined dependent to `remove`. No Short Title is named, the tool's print contract is unchanged, the channel is the console, and picks cleared through tags alone trigger nothing. Tells the user at the moment it happens that the answer reached beyond its own block, in the identifier-free style every status line in the workflow already uses, at no tool or bookkeeping cost. Says nothing the commit diff does not: the user still has to open the diff to learn which picks went, so the line adds output without removing the lookup, and it stays silent about tag-driven and transitive strips the runner never named.

Beside `Answer recorded.`, the skill lists the Short Title of each block it passed to `remove` as an undermined dependent, one per line in the shape the annotating passes use for still-skipped questions, with no reason attached. Coverage is the runner-named dependents only, so picks cleared through `<depends-on>` tags or transitively are not listed; the names come from the runner's own judgment step; the tool's print contract is unchanged; the channel is the console. Names exactly the judgment calls, the one part of the cascade no tag records, at zero tool cost, since the runner already holds those names when it builds the `remove` call. The list is not "which questions lost their pick": tag-cleared and transitively cleared blocks are omitted, and whether every listed name in fact lost a pick depends on what `remove` does with a named dependent that carries no pick or matches no block (sibling questions); the names must also be carried from wherever the judgment step lands to the skill's reporting step.

As "Named dependents listed", but each line carries the Short Title and the one clause by which the runner judged that pick undermined. Coverage stays the runner-named dependents only, the tool's print contract is unchanged, and the channel is the console. The reason is the only information about the cascade that exists nowhere in git, and printing it is what lets the user catch a strip made on a misreading right away, and argue with it, before the next recommendation pass re-picks over the kept alternatives. The longest free-text success-path output of any single-question skill, inviting the narration the reporting steps forbid, while still blind to tag-driven and transitive strips; the stated reason is only as good as the judgment that produced it.

`remove` prints the id of every block it stripped, one per line in the order it stripped them (the ids `remove_question` already returns to its caller), and the skill relays that print beside `Answer recorded.` without reasons. Coverage is every pick the write cleared, judgment-named, tag-driven, and transitive alike; the channel is the console. Exact and complete by construction, including the transitive and tag-driven strips the runner never named and could not otherwise know, with no runner bookkeeping and no way for the list to disagree with what the document now holds. Breaks the tool's "a write prints nothing on success" contract stated at every site, so the `remove` tests that assert empty stdout, the help text, the answer core's contract sentence, and CLAUDE.md all change, and every other `remove` caller (the review skill's prunes, the answer core's step-5 cascade, the out-of-scope sweep) now receives output it must be told to discard.

The skill runs `list --without-recommendation` before and after the `remove` and prints beside `Answer recorded.` each id present after and absent before, one per line without reasons. Coverage is every pick the write cleared; the tool and its print contract are unchanged; the channel is the console. Full coverage of tag-driven and transitive strips with no change to the tool, its tests, or the contract sentence any other caller relies on. Two more tool calls per answer and a set difference the runner computes in prose, the kind of mechanical reconciliation the project has moved into the tool, with a wrong list possible wherever the runner slips; whether the before-view is already in hand depends on the means by which the runner sees the standing picks (sibling question).

As "Tool-printed full list", with the skill attaching its one-clause reason to each printed id it passed itself as an undermined dependent and marking the rest as cleared through tags. Coverage is every cleared pick; the channel is the console. The complete picture in one place: every pick that went, which ones went on the runner's reading of the answer and why, and which went mechanically, so a user can check both the judgment and its reach at once. Carries both costs at once, the tool's print-contract change with its test and documentation ripple and the longest output of any option, for a report whose mechanical half the commit diff already records.

As "Compared full list", with the skill attaching its one-clause reason to each listed id it passed itself as an undermined dependent and marking the rest as cleared through tags. The tool is unchanged; the channel is the console. The complete, explained picture without touching the tool or any other caller's contract. Two extra tool calls, a prose set difference, and the longest output, all added to the skill's reporting step; whether the before-view is already in hand depends on the means by which the runner sees the standing picks (sibling question).

Nothing is printed beyond `Answer recorded.`; instead the skill appends to the answer commit's body one trailer-shaped line per runner-named dependent (such as `Cleared-pick: Short Title — reason`) after the rationale or the lifted line. Coverage is the runner-named dependents, since the diff already names the mechanically stripped blocks; the tool is unchanged; the channel is git alone. Puts the judgment's reasons where revert-then-re-answer and a later reader look, in history, and capture's rule of dropping the trailing run of `Key: value` lines keeps them out of the rationale it distills. The user is not told at the time, which is the only moment a wrong strip is cheap to catch; the record leans on capture treating the new line as a trailer, and it alters the "body is the lifted line verbatim" contract of `Alternative-answer:` commits and the rationale-only body of `Manual-answer:` commits.

The skill both prints the runner-named dependents with their reasons beside `Answer recorded.` (as in "Named dependents with reasons") and records the same lines as trailer-shaped lines in the commit body (as in "Commit-body record only"). Coverage is the runner-named dependents; the tool is unchanged; the channel is console and git together. The user is told now and the reasons survive in history for a later revert or capture reading, each channel covering what the other cannot. Two renderings of the same judgment to keep in step across both skills, the most output of the console options, and the capture-body and narration costs together.

open-question.question: Where in the committed repository, if anywhere, is the replay's aggregate result recorded?
open-question.recommendation: The counts belong in the milestone record, where the completion procedure already writes aggregates and where milestone 38 put its own, with the finish summary free to restate them: a figure in CLAUDE.md or the claims page goes stale and overstates a one-off replay over a hand-built case set as a repeatable test, a results log is a new convention for a single run, and committing no figure gives up the one number the goal allows.
open-question.alternative: The replay task's **Verified:** bullets in the milestone's TASKS_DONE.md carry the aggregate counts (stale picks cleared, unaffected picks left standing, and whatever bar or margin applies); no file outside the milestone directory carries a figure, docs/ and CLAUDE.md describe the new behaviour without numbers, and the finish summary in milestones/README.md may restate the counts in one bullet as it did for milestone 38. Matches the rule milestone 38 recorded word for word (aggregates in the Verified bullets, no new file, docs and requirements carry none of the figures), so the figures land where the completion procedure already writes, with no new file, no new convention, and nothing a later editor has to keep in sync. The figures sit in a milestone-local file that nothing reads back, so docs/design-claims.md keeps saying no test of claims 6 and 16 has run, and a reader asking what the change actually did has to know which milestone's done list to open.

The replay task's **Verified:** bullets in TASKS_DONE.md carry the counts, and docs/design-claims.md additionally cites the aggregate result in one sentence beside the **Metric** line of the claim the replay measures (claim 6's count of decisions with an out-of-date reason, or claim 16's strip-on-doubt), with the page's opening sentence that no suite runs the other tests revised to admit a one-off measurement; CLAUDE.md carries no figure. Puts the first measured figure on the page whose purpose is to pair each claim with a test, so the claim about stale reasons stops being unmeasured, which is the motive the uncommitted harness note gives for wanting a results home at all. The page's metrics name repeatable tests and a one-off replay over a hand-built case set is not one, so the citation needs wording that does not overstate; the figure becomes a public number to revise or withdraw if a later replay or harness measures differently, and its fit depends on how the result-bar sibling settles, since a figure recorded as a shortfall sits awkwardly as evidence for a claim.

The replay task's **Verified:** bullets in TASKS_DONE.md carry the counts, and the CLAUDE.md invariant bullet that records this milestone's design (undeclared dependents named by the hand-answer runner, reconciled in the same remove, strip on doubt) states the aggregate result as part of its rationale, the form the "eight of ten milestone-19 dispatches" figure already takes there; docs/ carries no number. Places the figure exactly where a future editor tempted to simplify the hand-answer step away will read it, which is what the rationale layer of CLAUDE.md exists for, and follows a precedent the file already holds. A figure earns its place in an invariant only when it argues for keeping the design, so a mixed or short result has no honest home there and the option falls back to the done list alone; CLAUDE.md is editor-facing, so users and the claims page never see the number, and the file grows a figure nobody re-measures.

The replay task's **Verified:** bullets in TASKS_DONE.md carry the counts, the same figure is cited beside the measured claim's **Metric** line in docs/design-claims.md, and it is stated again in the CLAUDE.md invariant bullet's rationale, so three committed homes hold the one number. Serves every reader at once, the done list for the milestone record, the claims page for public evidence, CLAUDE.md for the editor's rationale, with no new file or convention. Three copies of one figure to keep consistent under the repository's own one-source-of-truth claim, each later replay owing three edits, and it inherits both single-page conditions: the claims page's one-off-versus-repeatable wording and CLAUDE.md's need for a result that argues for the design.

A new committed project-level file outside the milestone directory (which holds exactly its four files), for example a measurements page under docs/ or the aggregate results log the uncommitted harness note sketches, holds one aggregate-only entry per replay run: the date, the plugin commit replayed, the case count, the counts cleared and left standing, and the bar if any; the replay task's **Verified:** bullets, docs/design-claims.md, and CLAUDE.md point at that entry rather than restating figures, and later replays or a future harness append entries to it. Gives measurements a single durable home that later runs extend in place, so a figure is neither buried in one milestone's done list nor duplicated across pages, and it builds the results home the harness idea leaves open before the harness exists. Adds a new top-level artifact and convention for a single run and fixes the shape of a harness that is not yet a milestone; a file with a row shape invites case-level detail the privacy rule forbids whatever case set the sibling question settles on, and the log's worth hinges on a second replay ever being run.

No committed artifact carries the aggregate counts; the replay task's **Verified:** bullets and the finish summary state only that the replay ran over its case set and its verdict in words (met its bar, fell short, or which direction the measurement showed), while the figures stay in the gitignored temp/ notes and the conversation that ran them. Keeps every measurement artifact, aggregate or not, in one place outside the tracked tree, so no committed figure can go stale or be misread as a repeatable benchmark result, and nothing from the private source projects, even in sum, enters the repository. Gives up the one number the milestone goal explicitly allows to be committed, so once the temp/ notes rot the measured effect is unrecoverable, later milestones (the harness idea, a re-measurement) have no baseline to compare against, and the finish summary can say only that the replay ran, not how much it cleared or spared.

open-question.question: By what means does a hand-answer runner see the standing recommendations on the other open questions, so that it can judge which of them its answer undermines, given that the answer core's `locate` prints only the answered block and `answer-open-question-with-alternative` tells its runner never to read `open_questions.xml` itself?
open-question.recommendation: The undermining test reads each standing pick's rationale beside its recommended option's what-it-is text, which only a block-level view shows, and a whole read for reasoning only is the form the repository already gives every inline runner and the shared procedures they follow, so the two hand-answer skills join that class with no tool change and the analyse step at last sees the siblings it asks about; the tool-only purity given up was a local sentence written when the skills needed nothing but their own block.
open-question.alternative: The runner reads `<MILESTONE_DIR>/open_questions.xml` whole with the file-reading tool, for reasoning only, and judges the standing picks from that read; the view holds every block, bare, alternatives-only, and pick-bearing alike, with its `<alternative>`, `<applied-principle>`, `<depends-on>`, and `<recommendation>` children. The "never read or edit it yourself" sentence of `answer-open-question-with-alternative`, the "every read and write of it in the core is a tool call" statement of `answer-open-question`, and the answer core's opening contract if the step lives there, are reworded to the invariant's form: a whole read is for reasoning only, and every locate, list, lift, and write is a tool call. The tool is unchanged. No tool change, and the exact wording five other inline skills already carry (the recommendation pass, the answer sweep, the review, `discuss-open-question`, `modify-milestone-goal`); the one read also gives the core's analyse step, which today asks about mooted and forced siblings it cannot see, the sibling blocks it reasons about, and it shows the `<depends-on>` tags, so the runner can tell a dependent the tool reconciles on its own from one it must name. It is the only option that moves a hand-answer skill from tool-only reads to a direct read, and if the judgment step lands in the shared answer core (the axis the judgment-home sibling owns) that direct read enters a procedure whose opening contract is that every read is a tool call and reaches its two other followers; the view is also the largest of any option, most of it bare blocks and advantage/drawback text that bears nothing on which picks the answer undermines.

The runner runs `walk` to get the id of every block carrying a `<recommendation>`, then one `locate` naming all of them but the answered one, and judges from the verbatim pick-bearing blocks that call prints; both skills' sentences banning a direct read stay as they are, and the tool is unchanged. Stays entirely inside the tool-only contract with two existing calls: `walk` is already the tool's only filter for pick-bearing blocks and `locate` already takes several titles, and the verbatim blocks show each pick with its rationale, its `<depends-on>` tags, and its kept alternatives, so the runner sees both what a pick assumed and which dependents the tool reconciles anyway. `walk` exists for the sweep's ordering, so the view leans on its filter as a side effect that no sentence of the tool promises for this purpose; and the print is nearly as long as the whole document, every alternative with its advantage and drawback for every pick-bearing block, while the bare and alternatives-only blocks the analyse step asks about stay unseen.

The runner runs `walk`, then `lift` once per id it prints with the answered one excluded, and judges from the one-line "`<option>` — `<rationale>`" prints; both ban sentences stay, and the tool is unchanged. The most compact view the tool gives today: one line per pick holding exactly the option and rationale an undermining test judges, in the same form the sweep would fold into `## Decisions`, so the runner sees precisely what a stale pick would record if left standing. One call per pick-bearing block, each written out in full, which is exactly the loop where a runner reaches for the variable or function the tool-command rule forbids; and the line carries no `<depends-on>` tag and no alternatives, so the runner cannot tell a dependent the tool reconciles anyway from one it must name, nor see what the pick chose against.

The tool gains a one-call view of the standing picks, a `list` flag beside `--with-question` or a subcommand, printing one line per block carrying a `<recommendation>`: its id, a tab, then its option and rationale as `lift` prints them; the runner judges from that print. Both ban sentences stay. It is a tool change: code, help text, tests under both pytest runs, golden fixtures, and a hosts rebuild. One call, inside the tool-only contract, printing exactly the fields the judgment needs and nothing else, in the shape `list --with-question` already set, and available unchanged to any later runner that needs the same view. A new subcommand or flag and a new print format to specify, test at both interpreters, and hold stable, bought for a view two existing calls already compose; and, like `lift`, the line shows no `<depends-on>` tag unless the format is widened to carry it, so the runner still cannot see which dependents the tool reconciles on its own.

The runner never sees a standing pick. It runs `walk` for the ids of the pick-bearing blocks and `list --with-question` for every block's question text, and names, among the pick-bearing questions, those its answer bears on judged from their question text alone, leaving the tool to strip whatever pick they carry; both ban sentences stay, and the tool is unchanged. Two short calls already in the plugin's vocabulary and the smallest print of any option, with no pick text entering the runner's context; it takes "doubt strips" to its end, since a runner that cannot see a pick cannot keep one it merely believes survives. Without the option or rationale the runner can apply no pick-level undermining test (the axis the undermined-pick-test sibling owns), only a bears-on-the-question test, so a pick on a question the answer touches but does not undermine is stripped as well and the replay counts every such pick against the change; it also sees no `<depends-on>` tag, so it may name dependents the tool reconciles already.

open-question.question: When a hand answer records the same option that the answered question's own standing recommendation names, does the runner still judge the other questions' standing picks against that answer?
open-question.recommendation: The judgment is against the decision as recorded, not against where its option came from: a confirming answer still writes text into Decisions that a sibling pick's rationale may contradict, as the one stale case in this repository's own history did through a confirming alternative answer undermining a pick from the same run, and every skip variant leaves that case standing, while a text-anchored test strips nothing from a pick formed coherently with the confirmed option, so the confirmation costs nothing where the picks were sound.
open-question.alternative: A match is no exemption: on every hand answer the runner performs the undermined-pick judgment over the other questions' standing picks against the recorded answer, whether or not the option it records is the one the answered block's own <recommendation option> names, through both the literal and the alternative skill, with no provenance condition. The answered block's own recommendation plays no part in deciding whether the judgment runs. One rule with no special case, and the only unconditional position that reaches a sibling pick formed in an earlier recommendation run than the answered block's own pick (a question added by a later review, or re-picked after a strip, as milestone 41's two `Recommendation-annotation:` runs show), which never had that pick in view and to which the confirmation is new information. The same decision clears different picks depending on which skill records it, since `/answer-open-question-with-recommendation` records the identical option with no judgment; in the common case where every pick came from one run, anything the judgment finds is a same-pass conflict the goal puts out of scope, and because doubt strips, picks that were in fact formed with the answer in view can lose their pick to a mere confirmation and cost a recommendation re-run.

When the option the runner hands to `remove --option` (the lifted alternative id, or for a literal answer the one verdict step 4 of the answer core forms) equals the answered block's <recommendation option>, the undermined-pick judgment is skipped outright and the answer proceeds exactly as the recommendation path does: `remove --option` reconciles the <depends-on>-tagged dependents and nothing else. No provenance condition; a literal answer's text beyond the option is not examined. The same decision is treated the same way whichever skill records it, confirming a pick costs nothing beyond the recording, and the match test reuses a verdict the answer core already forms, so no new judgment is added to the answer path. A sibling pick formed before the answered block's pick existed never had it in view and stands unexamined, which is the stale-pick pattern this milestone exists to close; and because `discuss-open-question` routes a user who agrees with the standing pick onto `/answer-open-question` naming the matching alternative id, the skipped case includes free-text answers whose constraints beyond the option are the deliberation's own and reach no other pick.

Only an exact match skips: `/answer-open-question-with-alternative` skips the undermined-pick judgment when the alternative id it lifted equals the answered block's <recommendation option>, and `/answer-open-question` always performs the full judgment, even when step 4's verdict passes the recommended option as `--option`. No provenance condition. The skip fires only where "the same option" is a fact rather than a verdict, since the alternative path records the option's own what-it-is text and nothing more, and the literal skill keeps one uniform behaviour with no second judgment about whether its free text matches. The literal path is the one `discuss-open-question` routes an agreeing user onto, so the commonest confirmation still pays the full judgment and its strip-on-doubt cost, while the alternative path still skips over a sibling pick formed in an earlier run that never had the answered block's pick in view.

The match narrows the judgment instead of skipping it: when the recorded option (lifted id or step-4 verdict) equals the answered block's <recommendation option>, the runner judges the other picks only against what the answer records beyond that option's own what-it-is text. For an alternative-id answer that surplus is empty and no pick is judged; for a literal answer it is the constraints or scope the text adds. No provenance condition. Catches the one thing a matching answer makes genuinely new to the standing picks, the deliberation's added constraints, without re-judging the option the picks are presumed to have had in view, so a confirmation strips only what its surplus undermines. Needs the runner to separate the option from the surplus in free text, a second judgment beside step 4's, where doubt about what counts as surplus means more stripping; and the option part still goes unjudged against a sibling pick formed in an earlier run that never had it in view.

The match skips the judgment only when the record shows it safe: the runner skips when the recorded option (lifted id or step-4 verdict) equals the answered block's <recommendation option> and no other standing pick was embedded by an earlier `Recommendation-annotation:` run than the answered block's own pick, so every one of them had that pick in view; when any standing pick predates it, the full judgment runs. A literal answer's surplus is not examined on a skip. Skips exactly when every pick was formed with the answered pick in view and judges exactly when some pick was not, so neither the confirmation cost of always judging nor the stale-pick gap of always skipping arises. The document carries no record of which run embedded a pick, and the `Recommendation-annotation:` commit body lists lift lines without Short Titles, so the condition is read only from commit diffs on a document a separate `Question-ordering:` commit reorders, the heaviest read any answer path would make; whether that read is practicable turns on the means by which the runner views the standing picks, and a literal answer's added constraints still reach no pick on a skip.

Combines the provenance condition with the exact-match rule: `/answer-open-question-with-alternative` skips the judgment only when its lifted id equals the answered block's <recommendation option> and no other standing pick predates that pick's `Recommendation-annotation:` run; `/answer-open-question` always performs the full judgment, and so does the alternative skill whenever any standing pick predates. The narrowest skip of the set: it fires only where the recorded option is a fact and every pick is known to have had it in view, so no judgment is ever skipped on an inference about free text or about what a pick saw. Pays the commit-history read for a skip that fires rarely, since confirming the standing pick through the alternative skill is the less common route, while literal confirmations always pay the full judgment and its strip-on-doubt cost; the read's practicability turns on the means by which the runner views the standing picks.

Combines the provenance condition with the narrowed judgment: when the recorded option (lifted id or step-4 verdict) equals the answered block's <recommendation option> and no other standing pick predates that pick's `Recommendation-annotation:` run, the runner judges only the answer's surplus beyond the option's what-it-is text (nothing, for an alternative-id answer); whenever any standing pick predates, the full judgment runs. The most precise position: nothing the picks had in view is judged twice, and nothing new to them, whether an earlier-run pick or a literal answer's added constraints, goes unjudged. Two mechanisms in one prose skill, a commit-history read and a judgment separating option from surplus in free text, the most rules to state and the most judgment calls per answer; the first turns on the means by which the runner views the standing picks, the second strips more wherever what counts as surplus is in doubt.

open-question.question: Should `/modify-milestone-goal` clear the standing recommendations that a goal revision undermines, and if it does, are the picks that declared a dependency on a cleared pick through a `<depends-on>` tag cleared along with it?
open-question.recommendation: A goal revision is the one event that can undermine many picks at once and the skill already computes which, so discarding that analysis leaves the stale picks for the sweep in any headless chain, while clearing them in the same run with the tool's existing multi-title strip call needs no tool change and treats dependents exactly as the recommendation pass's own re-pick hatch does: a tag records what a dependent assumed, the stripped block is re-picked under the new goal, and the answer-time cascade reconciles the tag, so a dependent whose pick is sound is not cleared for having declared one.
open-question.alternative: In the same run as the goal edit, the skill names the standing picks its impact analysis judges the revision undermines, from its whole read of `open_questions.xml`, and clears them with one `strip --recommendation` call over those Short Titles, keeping every `<alternative>`; a block whose `<depends-on>` names a cleared block keeps its pick and its tag, exactly as the tool's `strip` leaves it today; `open_questions.xml` joins `requirements.md` in the `Goal-revision:` commit. The tool as it stands does the write, since `strip --recommendation` already takes several titles, and dependents are treated as the recommendation pass's own re-pick treats them: a tag records what a dependent assumed, and the answer-time `remove --option` reconciles it. A dependent's pick goes on standing on an assumption about a block that no longer carries a pick; until that block is re-picked and answered, `walk` ignores the tag and the sweep can record the dependent first. Its reach turns on the test by which a pick counts as undermined, if the goal revision reuses the test a sibling settles for hand answers.

`/modify-milestone-goal` keeps editing `## Goal` alone and committing `requirements.md` alone under `Goal-revision:`; its step-3 impact analysis stays unwritten and unprinted, and no standing pick is cleared on a revision's account, now or later. A pick the revision undermines is cleared only by the user running the `strip --recommendation` hatch by hand, by review's pruning of a block the revised goal made moot (whose bare `remove` strips tagged dependents), or by the answer-time `remove --option` cascade. Preserves the recorded act-only invariant and keeps the one skill that edits the goal free of a judgment no automated test can check; no tool change, no second commit path, no new console output. The one event that can undermine every pick at once leaves them all standing, and a sweep run before anyone acts records them as given, which is the failure the milestone exists to stop; the analysis that already names the undermined picks is computed and discarded.

The skill still writes `requirements.md` alone and never touches `open_questions.xml`, but beside its `Goal revised.` line it prints the standing picks its impact analysis judges the revision undermines, each by Short Title, with the `strip --recommendation` command naming them ready to run; whether to add tagged dependents to that command is left to the user at the hatch. Keeps the skill act-only on the question document while the impact analysis stops being thrown away; the user decides what is cleared, so no sound pick is lost to a wrong judgment. Nothing is cleared until someone acts: in a headless chain the advisory has no reader and the stale picks ride into the sweep; it also adds a second kind of console output to a skill whose success path is one fixed line. Which picks it names turns on the test by which a pick counts as undermined, if the goal revision reuses the test a sibling settles for hand answers.

As "Clear undermined, dependents stand", but the clearing follows `<depends-on>` tags: every block whose tag names a cleared block is stripped of its pick as well, and so on over their dependents, so no tag is left naming a pick-less block, the guarantee `remove` gives; `<alternative>` elements are kept throughout and `open_questions.xml` joins the goal edit in the `Goal-revision:` commit. One reconciliation rule for every cascade: a pick never stands on an assumed sibling pick that is gone, so the sweep cannot record a dependent formed on a cleared assumption, whatever order the passes run in. No tool call strips transitively without removing a block, so either `strip --recommendation` gains a transitive form (a tool change with tests and rebuilt host trees) or the runner follows the tags by hand from its whole read; and a dependent whose pick is sound in itself loses it for having declared a tag, the case the recommendation pass's re-pick deliberately leaves standing. Its reach turns on the test by which a pick counts as undermined, if the goal revision reuses the test a sibling settles for hand answers.

Any committed goal revision clears the `<recommendation>`, `<depends-on>`, and `<applied-principle>` children of every block in the document, with no judgment of which picks the revision bears on, keeping every `<alternative>`; transitivity does not arise because nothing with a pick is left; `open_questions.xml` joins the `Goal-revision:` commit. No undermined test, no judgment prose, nothing to misjudge: every pick was formed against the old goal and the revision says so by clearing them all, a deterministic rule the tool can carry and the tests can check. A wording-only revision costs a full recommendation pass re-run and discards every sound pick, including ones the user has already read and agreed with, making goal revision expensive enough to discourage.

`/modify-milestone-goal` stays exactly as it is; the reconcile step of `/review-milestone-requirements`, the skill the goal revision already points at, gains the duty to strip, with `strip --recommendation`, every standing pick that the goal as it now reads undermines, judged from review's whole read of both documents; a block whose `<depends-on>` names a stripped block keeps its pick and its tag; the strip rides in review's own commit. Clearing lives in the loop engine that already reads both documents whole and judges staleness after every edit, so it catches picks undermined by any goal change however it arrived, and the goal skill's act-only invariant stays untouched. Nothing clears until review runs, so a sweep between revision and review records the stale picks; review judges against the current goal without the before-and-after the revision skill held, and its tidy step today acts only on evidence it can cite and flags on doubt, so this adds a judgment duty it now refuses. Its reach turns on the test by which a pick counts as undermined, if review reuses the test a sibling settles for hand answers.

As "Review clears, dependents stand", but review's strip follows `<depends-on>` tags over dependents and their dependents, as its bare `remove` of a pruned block already does, so no tag is left naming a pick-less block; `<alternative>` elements are kept throughout. Review's two cascades, pruning a block and stripping an undermined pick, then behave alike, and once review has run no dependent stands on a cleared assumption. Carries the same deferral as the non-transitive review path, and no tool call strips transitively without removing a block, so the tool changes or the runner follows the tags by hand; dependents whose picks are sound in themselves are cleared by propagation. Its reach turns on the test by which a pick counts as undermined, if review reuses the test a sibling settles for hand answers.

open-question.question: Which historical stale-pick cases does the replay cover: only the cases found in this repository's own milestone history, or also the cases found in other local projects that use the workflow?
open-question.recommendation: Fourteen labelled pairs across eight windows is the whole known population of the pattern against one pair here, and those windows also hold the many unaffected standing picks the collateral count needs, so both counts are measured on real material at eight headless runs per version rather than seventy-four, with only aggregates ever committed as the goal already requires; the goal-revision windows among them are replayable because a revision now clears the picks it undermines.
open-question.alternative: The replay covers the stale-pick cases already found in every local project that uses the workflow: the eight windows (fourteen pick-versus-decision pairs) the sweep-contradiction analysis identified, one in this repository and seven across three other local projects, with one of those windows alone holding six pairs from a single hand answer. Each is replayed from a scratch clone of its own repository at the parent of each hand answer, and no other windows are added. The whole known population of the pattern, fourteen labelled pairs rather than one, including the six-pair window that is the very case the milestone exists to prevent. Three of the four repositories are private, so the replay runs only on a machine holding them and nothing of its per-case material can enter a committed artifact; half the pairs come from one window, so a single case weighs half the stale count; and windows whose staleness came from a goal revision hinge on the sibling decision on goal-revision pick clearing.

The replay covers only the stale-pick cases already found in this repository's own milestone history: the one window the sweep-contradiction analysis identified, in milestone 37, where the standing pick on "Milestones root and cold start" (annotated 12:05) was undermined by `Alternative-answer: Failure cleanup scope` (12:14) and recorded stale by the sweep at 12:19. The window is replayed as the hand answers it holds, in commit order, each from a scratch clone at that answer's parent commit. No other local project is read and no further window is added. Every input lives in this public repository, so the replay can be rerun from any clone by anyone, with the case set fixed by a commit list rather than by access to private repositories. One window with one stale pair, so both counts rest on a single case; that window also holds two further manual answers and two goal revisions, and whether the goal revisions can be replayed at all hinges on the sibling decision on goal-revision pick clearing.

The replay covers every hand-answer window in this repository's own XML-era history, whether or not a stale pick was ever reported in it: each `Manual-answer:` or `Alternative-answer:` commit on an `open_questions.xml` that landed while another block carried a standing recommendation, selected by that rule rather than by the analysis's list, which is thirteen windows across milestones 27 to 41 at present. No other local project is read. Thirteen public windows, twelve of them with no reported stale pick, so the count of unaffected picks left standing (the side that "doubt strips" can get wrong) is measured on real hand answers without reading any private repository, and the set is reproducible by rule from a clone. Only one of the thirteen windows carries a known stale pick, so the count of stale picks cleared still rests on one pair, and the twelve windows without a contradiction report can be scored only by whatever record the sibling decision on replay ground truth settles on.

The replay covers every hand-answer window, whether or not a stale pick was ever reported in it, in every local project that uses the workflow: each `Manual-answer:` or `Alternative-answer:` commit on an `open_questions.xml` that landed while another block carried a standing recommendation, selected by that rule rather than by the analysis's list, which is seventy-four windows at present, thirteen in this repository and sixty-one across four other local projects. Each is replayed from a scratch clone of its own repository at the parent of the hand answer. The largest sample on both sides: all fourteen known stale pairs plus some sixty windows where the answer bore on no standing pick, so the cost of "doubt strips" is measured where it would actually show. Seventy-four headless runs of the skill under test per plugin version replayed, over four private repositories that must be present locally and whose material can never enter a committed artifact; the sixty-odd windows without a contradiction report can be scored only by whatever record the sibling decision on replay ground truth settles on.

open-question.question: In a replayed case, by what record is each standing pick classed as stale or as unaffected, so that the count of stale picks cleared and the count of unaffected picks left standing can both be taken?
open-question.recommendation: The labels must encode the milestone's own text-anchored definition of undermining, which no automated record applies: the historical advisory names only contradictions with a recorded entry and measured no misses, later history holds almost no corrections, a counterfactual re-pick is nondeterministic and cannot class a pick whose option survives but whose rationale rested on the answer, and an uncalibrated judge should gate nothing; over eight windows the picks are few enough to read by hand, fixed in the manifest before any run as milestone 38 fixed its cases, with private text never leaving that manifest.
open-question.alternative: The maintainer reads each case at the parent of its hand-answer commit — the decision that answer folded beside every standing pick's option and recommendation text — and labels each pick stale or unaffected by the milestone's own definition, writing the labels into the case manifest before any replay run and never changing them afterwards. No automated record supplies a label; the historical advisory and later history serve at most to point at candidates. The label applies the definition the milestone sets, independent of any detector's blind spots, and covers picks the sweep's advisory never named, runs that predate the advisory, and runs that printed no verdicts. Labour grows with the picks per case (one historical case had 26 picks standing), the labels are one reader's judgment with no agreement figure, made by the person who also wrote the rule under test, and labels on cases from other local projects quote private decision text, so they can never leave the local manifest; which notion of undermining the labels encode is the "Undermined pick test" sibling's to settle.

A standing pick is classed stale when the historical answer sweep that followed the hand answer reported it in a contradiction pair against the `## Decisions` entry that hand answer folded, and unaffected when that sweep recorded it with no such pair. The labels are read from the sweep run's session transcript and fixed before any replay run; no new judgment is formed per pick. The record already exists for every historical case in which the pattern was found, was formed at the time with the whole `requirements.md` in view, and cannot be shaped by what the new skill clears, so the replay needs no labelling step of its own. The advisory is a terminal-only model judgment of varying format that survives nowhere but in session transcripts: it exists only for runs after 2026-09-23, is absent where a run printed progress counts instead of per-question verdicts, measured no false negatives, and names a pick only when it contradicts a recorded `## Decisions` entry, so every unnamed pick is classed unaffected by default and a pick the new skill rightly clears on grounds the "Undermined pick test" sibling may settle on counts against it as an unaffected pick wrongly cleared; for cases from other local projects those transcripts are private material.

A standing pick is classed stale when the project's git history after the sweep shows its recorded decision overridden — a later question raised to revise the entry and answered the other way, a `Manual-answer:` rewriting the entry, a revert — or the completed tasks following the hand answer's decision over the pick's, and unaffected when the decision stood unchanged through the milestone's finish and its tasks. The labels are read from commits and shipped files and fixed before any replay run. It classes picks by what the project actually settled on, from a durable record in git rather than a terminal line, so a pick is called stale only when it demonstrably lost; for this repository's own cases that record is public. In 14 of the 21 analysed runs the next step was task derivation with the reported pairs untouched, no affected repository holds a revert, and the three traced conflicts were resolved silently during implementation in both directions, so most stale picks left no correction in history and would be classed unaffected; reading the shipped work per pick is itself a judgment that varies by reader, and history also records revisions made for unrelated reasons.

Each standing pick is classed by a fresh no-tools model session handed the hand answer's folded decision and the pick's option and recommendation text, blinded to which skill version is under test and to what the replay cleared, returning stale or unaffected as one line; verdicts are cached per pick and no human label is taken at any point. Classes every pick in every case at the same cost, is repeatable on resample, and extends unchanged to new cases, so both counts can be taken over the whole case set without hand labour. It is the same kind of model reading the skill under test performs, so the two may share blind spots and the counts measure agreement between two model judgments rather than correctness; the earlier one-off harness recorded that an uncalibrated judge's verdicts should gate nothing, and the judge's instruction still has to encode a notion of undermining that the "Undermined pick test" sibling owns.

The blind model judge of the previous option classes every standing pick, and the maintainer hand-labels a subset of picks drawn and fixed before the runs by the milestone's definition; the judge's agreement with that subset is reported beside the two counts, and the judge's labels stand only where agreement clears a bar fixed in advance, the hand labels being extended to all picks otherwise. Scales to every pick while giving the counts a measured error bar, which neither the bare judge nor the bare hand label provides. Two labelling mechanisms to build, run, and keep in step; on a small case set the calibration subset is small and its agreement figure correspondingly noisy; the hand subset carries the same private-text constraint as full hand labelling.

In the replayed clone, after the hand answer is recorded, every standing pick is stripped with the tool's `strip --recommendation` and the recommendation pass is run again with the new decision in view; a pick whose re-pick names a different option is classed stale and one whose re-pick names the same option unaffected, the classes read from the tool's `locate` of each block before and after. No human and no separate judge takes part. Operationalises the goal's own notion of a pick formed without the answer as a behavioural test — whether the pass picks otherwise once it sees the answer — using only the project's tooling and no reading of private decision text. The recommendation pass is nondeterministic (the earlier one-off saw an unchanged baseline move by one between identical rounds), so a changed option can be sampling noise and an unchanged one chance, making the class a label only over repeated samples at a full recommendation pass per case per sample; a pick whose option survives but whose rationale rested on the changed decision is classed unaffected whatever the "Undermined pick test" sibling settles.

The historical sweep's contradiction pairs supply the stale label for every pick they name, accepted without re-reading, and the maintainer hand-labels only the standing picks the advisory did not name, and every pick in runs where no advisory exists, by the milestone's definition, before any replay run. Spends hand labour only where the historical record is silent while catching the false negatives the advisory never measured, so the whole case set is covered at a fraction of full hand labelling. Mixes two notions of staleness in one count — the advisory's contradiction with a recorded entry for named picks, the milestone's definition for the rest — so the stale set is not uniform, and the named picks inherit the advisory's reading-dependent verdicts unchecked.

open-question.question: Is the replay's result a bar the milestone must meet before it can be finished, or a measurement that is reported whatever it shows?
open-question.recommendation: The goal names both counts and the design's two failure costs sit one on each, a missed stale pick becoming a wrong decision and an over-strip taxing every override, so a bar fixed before the runs on both is the only shape that commits to both before the figures are seen, while a bounded revision round and a recorded shortfall keep the milestone finishing with the change in place as milestone 38 did; a finish gate can hang on variance and a ship gate would withdraw a mechanism that is right by construction over fourteen pairs' noise.
open-question.alternative: A bar fixed before the runs on both counts: an absolute threshold on stale picks cleared and one on unaffected picks left standing, with no paired baseline run, since the unchanged hand-answer skills see only the answered block and so clear no undeclared pick and strip none. A shortfall on either count buys a fixed number of revision-and-re-run rounds of the judgment prose, the number set with the bar and possibly none; once they are spent the milestone finishes with the change in place and the shortfall recorded. This is the shape milestone 38 ran. The result is judged against a commitment made before it is seen, on both the benefit and the collateral, the milestone still always finishes, and the mechanics are already known from milestone 38's run. The bar binds only the rework, not the outcome: a change that misses it ships anyway, as milestone 38's did after its revision round left the margin unmoved, each extra round is another full replay of headless runs, and two thresholds on few cases double the chance that one case's run-to-run variance trips a round; its coarseness hinges on how many cases the replay covers.

No bar. The replay's two counts, stale picks cleared and unaffected picks left standing, are reported as they come out, and neither conditions the milestone's finish or the change staying in: the milestone finishes when its tasks are done, which is all `finish-current-milestone` checks today, and no value for either count is fixed in advance as something to meet. The figures are honest by construction and cost nothing beyond the runs: no threshold has to be chosen beforehand on a small, judgment-based case set, no rework or withdrawal hangs on run-to-run variance, and the milestone always finishes with the change in place while the design claim gets its first measured figure. Nothing fixed beforehand says what counts would have shown the change working or misfiring, so a weak result is interpreted after the fact and ships with no mandated response, and the replay's expense buys a number that binds nothing.

A bar fixed before the runs on one count only: the unaffected picks left standing must stay at or above a fixed floor, while the stale picks cleared are measured and reported with no threshold. A shortfall on the floor buys a fixed number of revision-and-re-run rounds set with the bar; after them the milestone finishes with the change in place and the shortfall recorded. It binds exactly the harm the goal names, picks the answer does not bear on being stripped, so it guards against a blunt runner without demanding a benefit figure from a small case set, and the milestone always finishes. It never asks whether the change catches anything, so a runner that strips nothing passes it, and the floor is only as crisp as the record that classes each pick, so its viability hinges on how a standing pick is classed as unaffected.

A bar fixed before the runs on one count only: the stale picks cleared must reach a fixed floor, while the unaffected picks left standing are measured and reported with no threshold. A shortfall on the floor buys a fixed number of revision-and-re-run rounds set with the bar; after them the milestone finishes with the change in place and the shortfall recorded. It binds the error the design's own asymmetry calls expensive, a stale pick left standing becoming a wrong recorded decision, and tolerates collateral strips, each costing one recommendation re-run, exactly as the goal's "doubt strips" already does. An over-stripping runner passes it, so the bar cannot catch the bluntness the goal also rules out, and the count it binds is small on the known material (fourteen pairs across eight runs), so the floor is coarse; how coarse hinges on which cases the replay covers.

A bar fixed before the runs on both counts, and the milestone is not finished until both are met: the replay task stays in `TASKS_TODO.md` with its acceptance unmet, which is the only mechanism available since `finish-current-milestone` checks nothing but an empty task list, and the judgment prose is revised and re-run with no fixed limit on rounds. The milestone is done only when the change has demonstrably both caught the stale picks and left the unaffected ones standing, the strongest guarantee any option gives. A judgment-based skill with run-to-run variance may never clear two thresholds at once on a small set, leaving the milestone open with no exit but lowering the bar after the fact or revising the goal, both of which undo the pre-registration; the risk hinges on how many cases the replay covers.

A floor fixed before the runs on the unaffected picks left standing only, with the stale picks cleared measured and reported without threshold, and the milestone not finished until the floor is met: the replay task stays open and the judgment prose is revised and re-run with no fixed limit on rounds. The change ships only once it is shown to leave unrelated picks alone, with no benefit threshold to chase on a small case set. The milestone waits on a count that one variance-driven collateral strip can flip, while a runner that strips nothing passes trivially, and whether a strip counts against the floor hinges on how a standing pick is classed as unaffected.

A floor fixed before the runs on the stale picks cleared only, with the unaffected picks left standing measured and reported without threshold, and the milestone not finished until the floor is met: the replay task stays open and the judgment prose is revised and re-run with no fixed limit on rounds. The change ships only once it is shown to catch stale picks, the error the design treats as the costly one, and nothing short of that closes the milestone. The floor can be met by over-stripping, and chasing a catch count on a handful of known pairs by revising prose without bound invites tuning the wording to those cases; the exposure hinges on which cases the replay covers.

A bar fixed before the runs on both counts, with a fixed number of revision-and-re-run rounds set with the bar and possibly none; a shortfall that persists after them withdraws the change, its skill and tool edits reverted, and the milestone finishes recording the withdrawal and the figures. Nothing reaches the plugin's users unless the evidence supports it on both the benefit and the collateral, and the milestone still closes instead of hanging. The milestone can finish with its first paragraph undone, on a verdict from a small judgment-based set where one case's run-to-run variance can decide whether the work is kept; how decisive one case is hinges on how many cases the replay covers.

A floor fixed before the runs on the unaffected picks left standing only, with the stale picks cleared measured and reported without threshold, and a fixed number of revision rounds set with the floor; a shortfall that persists after them withdraws the change, its edits reverted, and the milestone finishes recording the withdrawal and the figures. A runner shown to strip unrelated picks never reaches users, while its benefit is still reported, and the milestone closes either way. A runner that strips nothing passes and ships, and whether real work is thrown away turns on how a standing pick is classed as unaffected.

A floor fixed before the runs on the stale picks cleared only, with the unaffected picks left standing measured and reported without threshold, and a fixed number of revision rounds set with the floor; a shortfall that persists after them withdraws the change, its edits reverted, and the milestone finishes recording the withdrawal and the figures. Only a change shown to catch stale picks ships, and one that merely adds judgment without catching any is withdrawn rather than kept on faith, with the milestone closing either way. An over-stripping runner ships, and real work is withdrawn on a coarse count taken from a handful of known pairs; the coarseness hinges on which cases the replay covers.
